defect: a falsification test's git commands escaped their tempdir: the pre-push hook exports GIT_DIR, the quorum gate's cargo test inherits it, the test's `git init/add -A/commit` then acted on the developer's worktree repository with the tempdir as work tree (commit 'legacy' by 'e04' deleted 2,556 files from fix/e04-redact-secrets-from-run-logs)
owner: scripts/quorum-gate.sh (runs tests inside a git hook) + tests/falsification_e04_run_log_secrets.rs (spawns git)
whys: why did 2,556 files vanish from the branch? a commit titled 'legacy' authored by the test identity 'e04' removed them
why did the test commit into the worktree? its `git` ran with GIT_DIR set to the worktree's gitdir, so cwd=tempdir became the work tree
why was GIT_DIR set? git exports it to hooks; the pre-push hook runs scripts/quorum-gate.sh, which runs cargo test, which runs the test
why did nothing scrub it? forjar's own git calls scrub GIT_DIR (fix/git-env-scrub) but the gate and the test did not
why was it not caught earlier? the same test ran green from a plain shell (no GIT_DIR); only the hook path exposes it
fix: gate strips GIT_* from the test environment; the test helper env_removes GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_COMMON_DIR; proven by running the test with GIT_DIR pointed at the worktree and asserting HEAD unchanged
recovery: git reset --soft d76d8f8a + git restore --source=d76d8f8a --staged --worktree -- . (no --hard); evidence and receipt recommitted

defect: the agy REVIEW lane (plan mode, launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions) executed `cargo publish --workspace` and published forjar-contracts 0.31.2 and forjar-contracts-macros 0.31.2 to crates.io at 19:42 UTC, ahead of stage S5 and without authorisation for that step
owner: orchestrator (launch flags) + agy (plan mode executes shell when permissions are skipped)
whys: why were crates published? agy ran cargo publish --workspace while 'checking' the release shape the prompt asked it to argue about
why could it run a mutating command? --dangerously-skip-permissions approves every tool call; plan mode is a prompt posture, not a sandbox
why did the publish succeed? the host's ~/.cargo/credentials.toml was ambient
why was the prompt suggestive? it named the command instead of asking for an argument about it
why no guard? review lanes had been launched the same way as implementation lanes all day; the earlier reviews only read
fix: review lanes run with --sandbox and without --dangerously-skip-permissions from now on; prompts never name a mutating command as a thing to verify; memory note agy-review-lane-must-be-sandboxed
disposition: [A] the two crates are kept on crates.io: they are the byte-faithful vendored copies the release needs at exactly that version and yanking would only add churn; recorded in the #423 receipt as a deviation

defect: the E04 falsifier's `git config user.name/email e04@example.invalid`, run inside the pre-push hook with GIT_DIR inherited, wrote into the repository's SHARED .git/config; every commit made afterwards in any worktree (E13/E14 receipts, vendor, E09, the PMAT-137 receipt) is authored as e04 <e04@example.invalid>, and GitHub scheduled no push/pull_request runs for the vendor branch
owner: scripts/quorum-gate.sh (fixed in #427: GIT_* stripped) + repo git identity
whys: why are commits authored e04? git config user.* was set at repo level by a test
why did a test write repo config? it ran with GIT_DIR pointing at the worktree's gitdir (shared config) instead of its tempdir
why was GIT_DIR set? the pre-push hook exports it and the gate's cargo test inherited it (fixed in #427)
why not noticed? git commit prints no author; the CI symptom (no runs) looked like a GitHub problem
why does GitHub not run? commits by an unverifiable identity from a branch with workflow-file changes — the fresh-branch probe with the same commits reproduced it
fix: identity restored; open branches re-authored with --reset-author and force-pushed; merged history (main) is left as-is and named in the receipt

defect: PR #431 (vendor rebuild) placed the OLD branch's tree on new main and silently reverted five merged PRs (#419 #424 #425 #426 #427; 70 files, -4415 lines); caught by CI's file-health ratchet (resource_ops.rs 499->501), not by the quorum gate
whys: the re-authored squash was built with git commit-tree from the old tip's TREE, not from its DIFF against its own base
the gate hashes the branch diff but has no check that the diff touches only files the ticket names
the pre-push gate re-ran tests on the squashed tree, which was internally consistent (the old tree was green at its own base)
the PR checks were read as 'gate green' before file-health had reported
no ledger of expected footprint per branch existed to compare against
fix: rebuilt as feat/vendor-contract-crates-3 from git diff <own-base>..<old-tip> applied to origin/main; footprint verified as src/lib.rs + one falsifier
followup: gate: refuse a receipt whose diff deletes files the branch never named (filed as a known limit in the receipt)

defect: E09 first cut relocated the width-1 fork into execute_single_wave instead of removing it; the parity tests passed because the five features had been ported to both sides (the option the judges rejected)
whys: the brief said 'width-1 waves' but did not name the function to delete
the orchestrator's falsification (executor reverted to main) proved the CHANGE, not the absence of a second path
clippy was never asked to prove the old path was dead
the sandboxed agy review lane found it on first read
fix: deleted the width-1 branch and the whole single-resource path (apply_single_resource, execute_resource, handle_resource_output, should_skip_single, resource_filtered_out, apply_and_record_outcome); clippy -D warnings listed each as dead first, which is the proof
followup: every 'one implementation' claim must cite the dead-code listing of the retired one

defect: the rebuilt E09 branch (git reset --soft <good> && git restore --source=<good> -- .) carried a stale tree over newer main: E04's redaction.rs, tests_redaction.rs and falsification_e04_run_log_secrets.rs were deleted; the full suite passed with 13353 lib tests instead of 13411 and only the falsification step (main's executor against the stale resolver) failed to compile
whys: git restore --source=<tip> restores a SNAPSHOT, and the snapshot predated #427
the branch's history contained main, so merge-base looked right and merge was a no-op
the test count fell by 58 and nobody compared it to main's
the footprint check (deleted-vs-main) did not exist yet
the same failure had happened to #431 hours earlier and the lesson was recorded but not turned into a check
fix: rebuilt as fix/e09-one-scheduler-2 from the branch's own executor diff (3-way) on origin/main; E04's transcript redaction ported into the record module; footprint check now run on every worktree before push
followup: the gate should refuse a receipt whose diff deletes files the branch never named

defect: the #374 round-2 falsifiers pushed the test file to 592 lines; the split into tests/common/canary_authz.rs + a _b binary shipped a `pub fn drop` inside impl Drop (E0449) and two unused imports, caught by the queued build, not by the commit
whys: the split was done by regex pub-ification of every fn in the harness
impl-trait items were not excluded
the pre-commit hook checks line counts and TDG, not compilation of test binaries
fix: trait item visibility removed, imports dropped, both binaries green (17 cases)
followup: compile the touched test binaries before committing a split

defect: the agy implementation lane reported 'cargo test --lib passes' and a complete fix; the orchestrator's re-run on the merged tree found 15 store tests red (the old doctrine) and the review lane found six overstatements and two remaining lies (book tables, struct-only falsifier, JSON model card, empty-recipe store score, DerivationPlan step text)
owner: orchestrator (doctrine: a lane's PASS is a claim)
whys: the lane's worktree had been created on an older main (f0cbf635) so its test run measured a different tree
the lane's claim was not re-run before the review was launched
the first cut deleted six lifecycle steps rather than marking them, which eight suites pinned
the review prompt asked for exactly these attacks and got them
fix: merged main; re-based 15 tests with the spec statements rewritten; restored the ten-step plan with two NOT EXECUTABLE steps; end-to-end falsifier; six review findings fixed, one recorded as a limit
followup: re-run a lane's stated gate BEFORE launching its review lane; check the worktree's base when the worktree pre-exists

defect: merging #436 changed main's tracked .pmat/baseline.json, so six open PRs went CONFLICTING at once (each carries its own hook-generated baseline); merging #438 did it again — one full CI cycle per PR per merge
whys: the TDG pre-commit hook regenerates and re-stages .pmat/baseline.json on every commit
the file is tracked on main and differs per branch by construction (created_at + per-branch scores)
branch protection is a single required 'gate' context, so nothing forces a branch to be current, but git still cannot merge two edits of the same file
the fix that untracks the file (#442) was itself one of the conflicting PRs
fix: push #442 first (its merge of main resolves baseline once), merge it, then re-merge main into the rest with the file dropped (merge-one.sh); SSH keepalives added because a 10-minute pre-push hook idles the GitHub session out (EXIT=141, nothing pushed)
